newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Italy backs Romania's efforts to gain NATO and European Union membership, Italian foreign ministry secretary of state Pierro Fassino said during an official visit.
He said that Italy wants NATO membership talks to start concomitantly with all candidates.
* Upper Senate's chairman Petre Roman, on an official visit to Spain, met Spain's King Juan Carlos, Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Foreign Minister Abel Matutes.
Spain supports Romania's bid to be invited to join NATO when the Alliance announces its first eastward expansion later this year, Matutes told Roman.
* Roman invited King Juan Carlos to visit Romania.
* Parliament's upper chamber, the Senate, discussed bill on wages of staff employed by the National Securities Commission and the Bucharest bourse.

* The government will draft a package of laws within the next two months to encourage foreign investors to come to Romania, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told a seminar organised by the Economist Group. He said direct foreign investment was Romania's only chance of economic revival.
The seminar brings together cabinet members and some 150 potential foreign investors.
* Exiled King Michael is expected to meet President Emil Constantinescu on Tuesday, at 1700 gmt, for a private dinner at Constantinescu's presidential palace.
* Education Minister Virgil Petrescu told a news conference he planned to decentralise the ministry's activities and to draft laws on the development of private secondary education.
